newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Rite Aid sees revs at $11 bln by 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Rite Aid sees revs at $11 bln by 1997.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp chairman Martin Grass said the expected $2.3 billion acquisition of Thrifty PayLess Holdings Inc will create a drug retailer with a broad national presence and $11 billion in revenue by next year.
"Size is important. It help us lower costs, helps us buy better and amortize costs over a much bigger base in terms of corporate overhead," he told Reuters in an interview.
Thrifty's corporate offices in Wilsonville, Ore. will be shut, Grass said, resulting in a loss of 740 jobs. He also said that few, if any, Thrifty executives will join Rite Aid.

Grass said Rite Aid held early discussions with Thrifty regarding an acqusition before it negotiated the $1.8 billion purchase of Revco D.S. Inc, a transaction that fell apart in the spring under Federal Trade Commission opposition.
The FTC argued that the market concentration of the combined companies would be anticompetitive.
The Revco deal was announced at the end of last November and was formally killed five month later.

Grass said Rite Aid has "talked with Thrifty seriously since early summer. At first we got involved with Thrifty, but then got involved with Revco. We got the sense that Revco shareholder were willing to make a deal very quickly and we pursued."
The Thrifty acquisition is the largest and latest lockup in U.S. drug retailers, where price demands of managed care and perscription benefit providers have pressed consolidation.
On this, Grass would only say, "Perscriptions are a big part of our business, so it was definitely a factor."
Revco is now in the middle of an unwelcome $15 per share bid for Big B Inc, a deal that recently showed signs of turning friendly.
Earlier this month, Revco signed a confidentiality agreement with Big B to more closely examine its books.
Other potential buyers also have confidentiality agreements with Big B, it said.
Also, J.C. Penney Co Inc's Thrift Drug unit announced in August the $285 million purchase of Fay's Inc.
Prescription drug sales account for 56 percent of Rite Aid revenue and 34 percent at Thrifty, Grass said, a level he expects will rise closer to the Rite-Aid proportion.
In a deal related to the Rite Aid/Thrifty transaction, Penney's Thrift Drug will close the acquisition of 200 Rite Aid stores in the Carolinas by January, Grass said.
He also said Thrifty has been offered a newly-created, eleventh board seat at Rite Aid, and has not yet responded.
